title: The litigation-side checked-field read, the fact columns it fills on legal_action and hearing, the source stamps and the unmapped field codes are not specified
source: Legacy RWB-E2-025 v1 (04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 2 Story Files v5/RWB E2 025 Extraction for the stage 2 and 3 document types v1.md), sections 4, 7, 11, 12, 13 and 19; FSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v3 A1.2 (FEAT-LIT-04, FEAT-LIT-05, FEAT-LIT-10, FEAT-LIT-16), A2.4.3.1, A2.5.3.1, A2.10 and A2.16.3.1 (BR-S4-004, BR-S4-005, BR-S4-016, R-LIT-16, R-LIT-44) and the SCR-19, SCR-20 and SCR-30 rows of its screen list; TSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v2 T3.0, T3.1 (DF-LEG-001 to DF-LEG-014, DF-LEG-024 to DF-LEG-029), T3.2, T4, T5.2, T5.3, T6.1 and T-A.1 (API-S4-001 to API-S4-005); RWB-P5-E2025-CON sections 11 and 12; context pack S4 (service row, ownership rows of S4, DP table short form); Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-01, DP-06, DP-07, DP-11, DP-13 and DP-19; work package B2-S4-022 story line for RWB-S4-E2025-APP
section: 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow; 7 Acceptance criteria AC1 to AC8; 8 Business rules BR1, BR4 and BR7; 11 Data; 12.1; 12.2; 12.7; 13 Solution plan; 16 Test cases
description: One combined row for the S4 slice of the legacy key. (1) The legacy story gives the litigation side one sentence and one in-process interface: section 4 step 9 says S4 and S2 read confirmed field values through DocumentFieldReader to fill the pack and the treatment record, section 12 publishes 'List<CheckedField> checkedFields(UUID caseId, String documentType)' with the members documentId, docVersion, fieldName, value, state and confidence, and section 19 puts the write into legal_action, hearing and treatment outside the key. No source says how that read behaves once it crosses the service boundary on the litigation side, and RWB-P5-E2025-CON fixes the transport, the path, the shapes and the state filter only for the document side. (2) TSD S4 T3.1 gives legal_action DF-LEG-001 to DF-LEG-014 and hearing DF-LEG-024 to DF-LEG-029 and none of them is a source document identifier, a document version or a type-table version, so the columns that carry the provenance of an applied fact are named by no source, although R-UNI-38 and CTL-08 require the version in force to be recorded with the value. (3) Twelve field codes of the six types name no litigation column - contract_no, party_names, contract_amount, contract_date, approval_no, approved_amount, approval_date, approval_level, title_doc_no, mortgage_amount, registration_date and land_office - and no source says whether they are carried on the legal action, left in the hub or dropped; filing_date meets filed_date only by a word. (4) No source gives the litigation-side masking rule for party_names: the legacy note limits unmasked values to SY-CASEWF and SY-AGENT, which excludes this service, so the story stores no personal value at all. (5) No source says which of two types wins when both return court_name, nor what the apply does when the same field arrives from two documents of the same type.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-025 section 4 step 9 ('S4 and S2 modules: read confirmed field values through DocumentFieldReader to fill the pack and the treatment record'), section 12 ('public interface DocumentFieldReader { List<CheckedField> checkedFields(UUID caseId, String documentType); } // CheckedField: documentId, docVersion, fieldName, value, state (OK, CONFIRMED, CORRECTED), confidence'), sections 11 and 13 (the six types and their 20 new field codes, DOCTYPE-2026.12, EXTRACT_ACCURACY_PASS) and section 19 ('Writing extracted values into legal_action, hearing or treatment'); TSD S4 v2 T3.1 field tables (legal_action DF-LEG-001 id to DF-LEG-014 status; hearing DF-LEG-024 id to DF-LEG-029 next_date; no source-document, document-version or table-version field), T3.2 (LOV-LEGAL-TYPE, LOV-LEGAL-STATUS, LOV-HEARING, LOV-HEARING-OUTCOME only) and T-A.1 (API-S4-001 POST /notices/{noticeId}/approve, API-S4-002 POST /cases/{caseId}/legal-actions, API-S4-003 GET /legal-actions/{legalActionId}, API-S4-004 PATCH, API-S4-005 POST hearings, none of them a checked-field read); FSD S4 v3 A2.4.3.1 (R-LIT-16, BR-S4-004), A2.16.3.1 (R-LIT-44, R-LIT-45, BR-S4-016) and the screen rows SCR-19 Litigation workspace, SCR-20 Enforcement workspace and SCR-30 Case documents; RWB-P5-E2025-CON sections 11 and 12 (CheckedField, CheckedFieldSet, GET /api/recovery/document/v1/cases/{caseId}/checked-fields, the state filter and the masking rule); context pack S4 (tables legal_action and hearing, five REST operations provided, zero events, one workflow LitigationWorkflow); Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-01, DP-11 and R5.4 class C
area: Contract use, data model and mapping of the litigation-side checked-field fill
owner_role: Tech lead of rwb-litigation with the P5 owner of the checked-field contract and the rwb-litigation data owner
proposed: Build against RWB-P5-E2025-CON and take the operation, the payload, the state filter and the masking rule from the contract, never guessing them; add source_document_id, source_doc_version and source_table_version to legal_action on the service's own Flyway sequence, named and typed like the T3.0 standard columns, together with the apply key of the legal action, the document ID, the doc_version and the table version; map only a field code onto a column of the same name and count the twelve unmapped codes as the difference recorded in the apply result; stamp the tableVersion of the answer the facts were written from; never store party_names. Confirm the column set with the rwb-litigation data owner and the operation with the P5 contract owner at the wave 2 contract freeze.

title: No source says how an extracted hearing_date becomes a hearing row, which hearing_type that row carries, or what the apply does to an action in a closed status
source: TSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v2 T3.1 (hearing DF-LEG-024 to DF-LEG-029: legal_action_id required, hearing_date required, hearing_type LOV-HEARING, outcome LOV-HEARING-OUTCOME, next_date), T3.2 (LOV-HEARING FIRST_HEARING, WITNESS, JUDGMENT_READING, MEDIATION), T3.3 (hearing many to 1 legal_action) and T4 (R-LIT-01 to R-LIT-25 and the 54 rows beyond); FSD S4 v3 A2.11 (Track hearings, deadlines and fees) and A2.16; legacy RWB-E2-025 v1 section 13 (COURT_NOTICE keeps court_name, black_case_no, notice_date and hearing_date) and AC9; context pack S4 (workflow LitigationWorkflow); work package B2-S4-022 story line for RWB-S4-E2025-APP
section: 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow step 6; 5 Exception paths; 7 Acceptance criteria AC2; 8 Business rules BR5; 9 State transitions; 12.5; 12.6; 13 Solution plan; 19 Out of scope
description: A hearing row cannot exist without a legal_action_id and a hearing_date, and its hearing_type is drawn from LOV-HEARING, but no source says what a hearing created from an extracted hearing_date of a COURT_NOTICE carries in hearing_type, whether an extracted date may create a second hearing on a date the action already holds, or whether it updates next_date of the open hearing instead. No source says either what the apply does when the legal action is in a closed status of LOV-LEGAL-STATUS (CLOSED, WITHDRAWN) or when the same date arrives twice from two documents: the litigation state machine of T4 is written in terms of events such as PROOF_OF_DELIVERY_RECEIVED and JUDGMENT_RECORDED and names no extracted-document event at all, and the FSD hearing feature A2.11 assumes a hearing recorded by a person. The story therefore fixes the rule itself and records it here rather than hiding it in code.
evidence: TSD S4 v2 T3.1 hearing table (DF-LEG-025 legal_action_id CROSS_REF required, DF-LEG-026 hearing_date DATE required, DF-LEG-027 hearing_type LOV varchar(20) with no default, DF-LEG-028 outcome, DF-LEG-029 next_date) and T3.2 (LOV-HEARING has four values and none of them means 'extracted' or 'unknown'); T3.3 (hearing many to 1 legal_action, so a second row on the same date is allowed by the model and forbidden by no constraint); TSD S4 v2 T4 (the LITIGATION machine of 79 rules over 38 states, triggered by named events and by no document event); FSD S4 v3 A2.11 (Track hearings, deadlines and fees) and A2.16 (Record the judgment); legacy RWB-E2-025 section 13 (COURT_NOTICE field list with notice_date and hearing_date) and section 7 AC9 (the reader returns checked fields to the litigation module); context pack S4 (zero jobs, one workflow LitigationWorkflow, tables legal_action and hearing)
area: Hearing creation, LOV-HEARING value and behaviour on a closed legal action
owner_role: Litigation business analyst with the rwb-litigation data owner and the S4 hearing story owner
proposed: One hearing row per legal action and hearing_date: if the action holds no hearing with that date, create one with hearing_type left empty and is_active true and record that the value came from an extracted document in the source stamps; if it holds one, update next_date only. A closed or withdrawn legal action accepts no fact at all and answers 409 with the conflict message of the baseline. Confirm the hearing_type policy with the litigation business analyst before the S4 hearing story freezes its shape, and treat the outcome of that confirm as the source of the rule in a later version.
